rows.title: Ayatul Kursi
rows.t: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most Hight, the Most Great.

rows.title: Al-Ikhlas
rows.t: Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One, (1) Allah, the Eternal Refuge. (2) He neither begets nor is born, (3) Nor is there to Him any equivalent." (4)

rows.title: Al-Falaq
rows.t: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak (1) From the evil of that which He created (2) And from the evil of darkness when it settles (3) And from the evil of the blowers in knots (4) And from the evil of an envier when he envies." (5)

rows.title: An-Nas
rows.t: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, (1) The King of mankind. (2) The God of mankind, (3) From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, (4) Who whispers in the breasts of mankind, (5) Of the jinn and mankind." (6)

rows.title: Upon Entering The Morning by Asking for Protection from Allah
rows.t: We have entered the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him is praise, and He is over all things competent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evil of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the Fire and the punishment of the grave.

rows.title: Upon Entering The Morning with The Grace of Allah
rows.t: O Allah, with Your grace and help we enter the morning, and with Your grace and help we enter the evening. By Your grace and will we live and by Your grace and will we die. And to You is the resurrection (for all creatures).

rows.title: Sayyid al-Istighfar
rows.t: O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no deity worthy of worship except You. You created me and I am Your servant. I will be true to my covenant and promise to You as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me and I acknowledge my sin, therefore, forgive me. Indeed, there is no one who can forgive sins except You.

rows.title: Dua for Protection and Good Health
rows.t: O Allah, protect my body (from illness and from what I do not want). O Allah, protect my hearing (from illness and disobedience or from what I do not want). O Allah, protect my sight, there is no deity worthy of worship except You. O Allah, indeed I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty. I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, there is no deity worthy of worship except You.

rows.title: Dua for Salvation in The World and Hereafter
rows.t: O Allah, indeed I ask You for well-being and safety in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, indeed I ask You for well-being and safety in my religion, my world, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my flaws (faults and things that are not appropriate for others to see) and calm me from fear. O Allah, protect me from the front, behind, right, left and above me. I seek refuge in Your greatness, so that I am not snatched from below me (by snakes or swallowed by the earth, etc., which would cause me to fall).

rows.title: Dua for Protection from Shaytan Whispers
rows.t: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord of all things and their Sovereign. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself, Satan and his soldiers (temptations to commit shirk against Allah), and I (seek refuge in You) from committing evil against myself or dragging it to a Muslim.

rows.title: Asking for Protection from All Harms
rows.t: In the name of Allah with Whose name nothing can harm on earth or in heaven, and He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

rows.title: Declaration of Pleasure with Allah, Islam, and the Prophet Muhammad sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam
rows.t: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, Islam as my religion and Muhammad sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam as my Prophet (sent by Allah).

rows.title: Asking Allah for Guidance
rows.t: O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, by Your mercy I seek help, rectify all my affairs and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.

rows.title: Entering The Morning Upon The Natural Religion of Islam
rows.t: In the morning we are upon the fitrah of Islam, the word of sincerity (the testimony of faith), the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and the religion of our father Abraham, who stood upon the straight path, a Muslim, and was not among the polytheists.

rows.title: Tawheed Dhikr
rows.t: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and all praise. And He is over all things competent.

rows.title: Read Tasbih
rows.t: Glory to Allah, I praise Him as many as the number of His creatures, Glory to Allah according to His pleasure, as pure as the weight of His Throne, and as pure as the ink (which writes) His words.

rows.title: Dua for Useful Knowledge, Good Sustenance, and Accepted Deeds
rows.t: O Allah, I really ask You for knowledge that is beneficial, sustenance that is lawful, and deeds that are accepted.

rows.title: Daily Tasbih and Tahmid
rows.t: Glory be to Allah, I praise Him.

rows.title: Istighfar 100x a Day
rows.t: I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.

rows.title: Ayat al-Kursi
rows.t: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great. Whoever recites this verse in the morning will be protected until the evening. And whoever recites it in the evening will be protected until the morning.

rows.title: Al-Ikhlas
rows.t: Say, "He is Allah , [who is] One, (1) Allah , the Eternal Refuge. (2) He neither begets nor is born, (3) Nor is there to Him any equivalent." (4) The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said: Recite Qul huwallahu ahad, and Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (Al-Falaq and An-Nas) in the evening and morning three times, and it will suffice you (protect you) from everything.

rows.title: Al-Falaq
rows.t: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak (1) From the evil of that which He created (2) And from the evil of darkness when it settles (3) And from the evil of the blowers in knots (4) And from the evil of an envier when he envies." (5) The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said: Recite Qul huwallahu ahad, and Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (Al-Falaq and An-Nas) in the evening and morning three times, and it will suffice you (protect you) from everything.

rows.title: An-Nas
rows.t: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, (1) The King of mankind. (2) The God of mankind, (3) From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, (4) Who whispers in the breasts of mankind, (5) Of the jinn and mankind." (6) The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said: Recite Qul huwallahu ahad, and Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (Al-Falaq and An-Nas) in the evening and morning three times, and it will suffice you (protect you) from everything.

rows.title: Entering the Evening in the Kingdom of Allah and Seeking His Protection
rows.t: We have entered the evening and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him is praise, and He is over all things competent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evil of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the Fire and the punishment of the grave. Seeking protection from evil is prioritized, the principle that shows the importance of this is: "Preventing harm is more important and prioritized than bringing about good."

rows.title: Entering the Evening by Seeking Allah's Mercy
rows.t: O Allah, by Your grace and help we have entered the evening, and by Your grace and help we enter the morning. By Your grace and help we live and by Your will we die. And to You is the final return (of all creatures). Everything we do from morning to evening, from the beginning of our lives until we die, is all under Allah's control and to Him we return.

rows.title: The Master of Seeking Forgiveness
rows.t: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no deity worthy of worship except You, You created me and I am Your servant. I will be true to my covenant and promise to You as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me and I acknowledge my sin, therefore, forgive me. Indeed, there is no one who can forgive sins except You. Whoever recites it with certainty in the evening, and then he dies, he will enter Paradise, and likewise if (recited) in the morning.

rows.title: Prayer for Health and Protection
rows.t: O Allah, protect my body (from illness and from what I do not want). O Allah, protect my hearing (from illness and disobedience or from what I do not want). O Allah, protect my sight, there is no deity worthy of worship except You. O Allah, indeed I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty. I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, there is no deity worthy of worship except You. By asking Allah to grant us well-being in our bodies, we ask to be healed from all physical and spiritual illnesses, so that we have a healthy body and a pure heart, and therefore use this healthy body in a way that pleases Allah.

rows.title: Prayer for Safety in This World and the Hereafter
rows.t: O Allah, indeed I ask You for well-being and safety in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, indeed I ask You for well-being and safety in my religion, my world, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my flaws (faults and things that are not appropriate for others to see) and calm me from fear. O Allah, protect me from the front, behind, right, left and above me. I seek refuge in Your greatness, so that I am not snatched from below me (by snakes or swallowed by the earth, etc., which would cause me to fall). The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, never left this supplication in the morning and evening. It contains protection and safety for religion, the world, family, and wealth from various kinds of disturbances that come from all directions.

rows.title: Prayer for Seeking Protection from the Whispers of Satan
rows.t: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord of all things and their Sovereign. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself, Satan and his soldiers (temptations to commit shirk against Allah), and I (seek refuge in You) from committing evil against myself or dragging it to a Muslim. The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said to Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, "Say it morning and evening and when you want to sleep."

rows.title: Remembrance to Be Protected from All Dangers
rows.t: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing in the earth or the heavens can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Whoever recites it three times in the morning and evening, nothing will harm him.

rows.title: Declaration of Contentment with Allah, Islam, and the Prophet Muhammad sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam
rows.t: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, Islam as my religion, and Muhammad, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, as my Prophet. Whoever recites it three times in the morning and evening, Allah will grant His pleasure to him on the Day of Resurrection.

rows.title: Asking for Guidance from Allah
rows.t: O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, by Your mercy I seek help, rectify all my affairs and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye. The meaning of this supplication is that humans are in dire need of Allah and pray that Allah does not abandon them even for a moment.

rows.title: Entering the Evening on the Natural Disposition of Islam
rows.t: In the evening we are upon the fitrah of Islam, the word of sincerity (the testimony of faith), the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and the religion of our father Abraham, who stood upon the straight path, a Muslim, and was not among the polytheists. 'Fitratil Islam' means upon the Sunnah, 'kalimatil ikhlas' means the testimony of faith, and 'hanifan' means a heart inclined towards the straight path and goodness.

rows.title: Remembrance of the Oneness of Allah
rows.t: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and all praise. He is over all things competent. Whoever says this dhikr 100 times a day, it is like freeing 10 slaves, 100 good deeds are recorded for him, 100 mistakes are erased for him, he will be protected from the disturbances of Satan from morning until evening, and no one is better than what he does except someone who practices more than that.

rows.title: Reciting Praise to Allah
rows.t: Glory be to Allah, as many as His creations, Glory be to Allah as much as His pleasure, Glory be to Allah as much as the weight of His Throne, and as much as the ink of His written words. The Prophet, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, told Juwairiyah that the dhikr above has surpassed the dhikr recited by Juwairiyah from after Fajr until Dhuha time.

rows.title: Daily Praise (Tasbih and Alhamdulillah)
rows.t: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him. Whoever says "Subhanallah wa bihamdihi" 100 times in the morning and evening, then nothing will come on the Day of Judgment better than what he has done except one who says the same or more than that.

rows.title: Seeking Forgiveness 100 Times a Day
rows.t: I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him. Ibn 'Umar said: The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said: 'O people, repent to Allah, for indeed I repent to Him one hundred times a day.'

rows.title: Prayer for Protection from the Evil of Allah's Creation
rows.t: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created. Whoever recites it three times in the evening, they will not be afflicted with fever that night.

rows.title: Istighfar
rows.t: I seek forgiveness from Allah. When the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times and recite the dhikr above. Al-Auza'i stated that the recitation of istighfar is 'Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah.'

rows.title: Allah, The Giver of Peace
rows.t: O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor. When the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times and recite the dhikr above. Al-Auza'i stated that the recitation of istighfar is 'Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah.'

rows.title: Allah, The Preventer and The Giver of All Things
rows.t: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs dominion and praise, and He is over all things competent. O Allah, there is no preventer of what You give, and no giver of what You withhold, and wealth and honor do not benefit their possessor (except faith and righteous deeds that save from punishment). Only from You is wealth and honor.

rows.title: Allah, The Possessor of All and The Only One Worthy of Worship
rows.t: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs dominion and praise, and He is over all things competent. There is no power and no strength except by Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and we do not worship except Him. To Him belongs all favor, grace, and good praise. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, making our religion sincerely for Him, even if the disbelievers dislike it. 'Abdullah bin Zubair said, "The Prophet, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, used to recite the tahlil (laa ilaha illallah) at the end of the prayer."

rows.title: Tasbih
rows.t: Glory be to Allah

rows.title: Tahmid
rows.t: All praise is for Allah

rows.title: Takbir
rows.t: Allah is the Greatest

rows.title: There is No Partner for Allah, and To Him Belongs All Things
rows.t: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs dominion and praise, and He is over all things competent. Whoever recites the dhikr above, his sins will be forgiven, even if they are as numerous as the foam on the ocean. Imam Nawawi, may Allah have mercy on him, said that the text of the hadith indicates that 'Subhanallah', 'Alhamdulillah', and 'Allahu akbar' are each recited 33 times separately.

rows.title: Ayat al-Kursi
rows.t: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great. Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after finishing the prayer, nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except death.

rows.title: Al-Ikhlas
rows.t: Say, "He is Allah , [who is] One, (1) Allah , the Eternal Refuge. (2) He neither begets nor is born, (3) Nor is there to Him any equivalent." (4) The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said: Recite Qul huwallahu ahad, and Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (Al-Falaq and An-Nas) in the evening and morning three times, and it will suffice you (protect you) from everything.

rows.title: Al-Falaq
rows.t: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak (1) From the evil of that which He created (2) And from the evil of darkness when it settles (3) And from the evil of the blowers in knots (4) And from the evil of an envier when he envies." (5) The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said: Recite Qul huwallahu ahad, and Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (Al-Falaq and An-Nas) in the evening and morning three times, and it will suffice you (protect you) from everything.

rows.title: An-Nas
rows.t: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, (1) The King of mankind. (2) The God of mankind, (3) From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, (4) Who whispers in the breasts of mankind, (5) Of the jinn and mankind." (6) The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said: Recite Qul huwallahu ahad, and Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (Al-Falaq and An-Nas) in the evening and morning three times, and it will suffice you (protect you) from everything.

rows.title: Supplication for Beneficial Knowledge, Good Provision, and Accepted Deeds
rows.t: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and accepted deeds. Beneficial knowledge is a provision that makes life easier, obtaining good provision is a person's goal in working, and accepted deeds are the hope of every person who performs good deeds. Therefore, a servant should always ask for these 3 things every morning before starting their various activities.

rows.title: Supplication Before Sleeping
rows.t: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. The Prophet, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, always started and ended his day with dhikr.

rows.title: Supplication Upon Waking Up
rows.t: All praise is for Allah who gives us life after He has caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection. By reciting the supplication above, a servant begins his day by praising the name of Allah, the Giver of Life and the Bringer of Death.

rows.title: Supplication Entering the Bathroom
rows.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil and the wicked. This supplication acts as a barrier between a servant's private parts and the jinn when entering the bathroom.

rows.title: Supplication Leaving the Bathroom
rows.t: I ask for Your forgiveness (O Allah). The bathroom is one of the homes of the jinn and devils, so it is recommended to ask for forgiveness for any mistakes, intentional or unintentional, made while in the bathroom.

rows.title: Supplication Before Eating
rows.t: In the name of Allah. The benefit of reciting Bismillah before eating is to prevent Satan from joining humans in eating.

rows.title: Supplication If Forgetting Bismillah at the Beginning of a Meal
rows.t: In the name of Allah, at its beginning and its end. Islam pays great attention to etiquette. If someone forgets to recite the supplication before eating at the beginning, it is still recommended to recite it in the middle, even if there is only a spoonful of rice left.

rows.title: Supplication After Eating
rows.t: All praise is to Allah who has fed me this and provided for me without any power or strength from me. The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, said that if someone recites this supplication, then his past sins will be forgiven.

rows.title: Supplication Entering the Mosque
rows.t: O Allah, open the doors of Your mercy for me. The mosque is the house of Allah; a servant should honor it and hope for Allah's mercy within it.

rows.title: Supplication Leaving the Mosque
rows.t: O Allah, I ask You for Your bounty. Allah's earth is vast, and there are many ways to seek provision. A servant should ask for Allah's bounty to be facilitated in obtaining the provision that Allah has distributed to all His servants.

rows.title: Supplication Before Performing Ablution
rows.t: In the name of Allah. It is prescribed to begin every important matter by saying Bismillah, whether it be an act of worship or otherwise.

rows.title: Supplication After Performing Ablution
rows.t: I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah, make me among those who repent and make me among those who purify themselves. Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise, I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You. Whoever recites this supplication, eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter from whichever gate he wishes.

rows.title: Supplication for Breaking the Fast
rows.t: The thirst has gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, Insha Allah. It is highly recommended for those who are fasting to increase their supplications before and after breaking the fast, because the supplication of a fasting person is one of the three supplications that are not rejected.

rows.title: Supplication Entering the House #1
rows.t: Peace be upon you. The greeting is a supplication of hope, a hope that you will be safe from all kinds of sorrow and suffering, and be enveloped in mercy and blessings.

rows.title: Supplication Entering the House #2
rows.t: Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. The greeting is a supplication of hope, a hope that you will be safe from all kinds of sorrow and suffering, and be enveloped in mercy and blessings.

rows.title: Supplication Leaving the House
rows.t: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah. There is no might nor power except with Allah. Whoever recites this supplication, it will be said to him: "You will be guided, sufficed, and protected." Satan will then depart from him. Another satan will say: "How can you harm someone who has been guided, sufficed, and protected?!"

rows.title: Supplication for Protection from Causing or Experiencing Harm Outside the House
rows.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You lest I should stray or be led astray, slip or be tripped, wrong or be wronged, or act foolishly or have foolishness done to me. When a person leaves the house, they will encounter all kinds of things, both good and bad, especially harm caused by themselves. Therefore, it is commanded to seek refuge from oneself and from others.

rows.title: Travel Supplication
rows.t: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. Glory be to Him who has provided this for us, though we could never have had it by our own efforts. Surely to our Lord we are returning. O Allah, we ask You for righteousness and piety in this journey of ours, and for deeds that please You. O Allah, lighten for us the hardship of this journey and quickly bring us to our destination. O Allah, You are our Companion on the journey and the Guardian of our families. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from a bad return, and from seeing something unpleasant concerning our wealth, family, or children. This supplication has two parts. The first is praise of Allah and the submission of the servant. The second is a request to Allah for ease in travel and in the affairs of what the servant has left at home.

rows.title: Supplication of a Resident for Someone Who is Traveling
rows.t: I entrust your religion, your trust, and the end of your deeds to Allah. Three priorities of a servant that must be maintained everywhere: religion, trust, and deeds, because a person will be resurrected according to their deeds.

rows.title: Supplication for Piety from a Resident to Someone Who is Traveling
rows.t: May Allah provide you with piety, forgive your sins, and ease goodness for you wherever you are. Piety is the best provision that a servant must prepare for the Hereafter, because there is no salvation except through piety.

rows.title: Supplication When Wearing New Clothes
rows.t: O Allah, to You is all praise. You have clothed me with this. I ask You for its goodness and the goodness for which it was made, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil for which it was made. By reciting this supplication, one asks that the clothes they have bought may provide goodness and also be a protection against various evils.

rows.title: Supplication When Wearing Clothes
rows.t: Praise be to Allah who has clothed me with this garment and provided it for me without any power or strength from me. The virtue of reciting this supplication is that past sins will be forgiven, Insha Allah.

rows.title: Supplication When Mounting a Vehicle
rows.t: In the name of Allah, in the name of Allah, in the name of Allah. All praise is to Allah. Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have done so by ourselves. And indeed, to our Lord we will return. Glory be to You, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for none can forgive sins except You. By reciting the supplication for mounting a vehicle, our journey will always be under the protection of Allah. In addition, we will also receive rewards, help, and a calmer heart.

rows.title: Supplication When it Rains
rows.t: O Allah, make it a beneficial rain. It is encouraged to pray when it rains so that goodness and blessings increase, as well as its benefits.

rows.title: Supplication During Heavy Rain
rows.t: O Allah, (let the rain fall) around us, not on us. O Allah, (let it fall) on the hills, mountains, small mountains, valleys, and places where trees grow. The supplication above is recited when the rain gets heavier or there is a concern that the rain will cause harm.

rows.title: Supplication After it Rains
rows.t: We have been given rain by the bounty and mercy of Allah. By reciting this supplication, one believes that rain falls by the will of Allah (Allah's virtue), not by the stars, so they do not become disbelievers in Allah.

rows.title: Supplication During Strong Wind
rows.t: O Allah, I ask You for the good of this wind, and I seek refuge in You from its evil. Among the signs of Allah's power is a strong wind that can bring blessings and punishment, namely good and bad. Therefore, a servant should continue to ask for good and seek refuge from all harm.

rows.title: The Best Supplication for Seeking Forgiveness (Sayyid al-Istighfar)
rows.t: O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no deity worthy of worship except You. You created me, and I am Your servant. I abide to Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your blessings upon me, and I acknowledge my sin. So forgive me, for none can forgive sins except You. Whoever recites it with certainty in the evening, and then he dies, he will enter Paradise, and likewise if (recited) in the morning.

rows.title: Supplication for Ease in All Matters
rows.t: O Allah, there is no ease except in that which You make easy, and You make the difficult easy if You wish. Ease comes only from Allah. Even something difficult can become easy Insha Allah.

rows.title: Supplication When Afflicted by Calamity
rows.t: Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me for my affliction and replace it with something better. A servant should recite the supplication above when afflicted by calamity with certainty and hope. Insha Allah, with this, they will receive a better replacement.

rows.title: Supplication When in Debt
rows.t: O Allah, suffice me with what is lawful and keep me away from what is unlawful, and enrich me with Your bounty so I do not depend on anyone besides You. Lawful provision, even if it is little, is better than abundant unlawful wealth.

rows.title: Supplication for Protection from Laziness, Sadness, and Debt
rows.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, and I seek refuge in You from incapacity and laziness, and I seek refuge in You from cowardice and miserliness, and I seek refuge in You from being overpowered by debt and from being overcome by men. Abu Umamah then narrated: After I practiced this supplication, Allah truly removed my anxiety and gave me the ability to repay my debt.

rows.title: Supplication After Sneezing
rows.t: All praise is to Allah. Indeed, Allah loves sneezing because it moves a person to worship. It is encouraged to respond to the praise of Allah by someone who praises Allah, and vice versa.

rows.title: Supplication Upon Hearing Someone Sneeze
rows.t: May Allah have mercy on you. Indeed, Allah loves sneezing because it moves a person to worship. It is encouraged to respond to the praise of Allah by someone who praises Allah, and vice versa.

rows.title: Response to Someone Who Says 'Yarhamukallah' After You Sneeze
rows.t: May Allah guide you and improve your condition. Indeed, Allah loves sneezing because it moves a person to worship. It is encouraged to respond to the praise of Allah by someone who praises Allah, and vice versa.

rows.title: Supplication for Good Character
rows.t: O Allah, just as You have made my external form good, make my character good as well. A charming appearance is not enough provision for a Muslim, but it must be accompanied by noble character. Therefore, a Muslim should constantly ask for their character to be improved and beautified.

rows.title: Prayer for Protection from Satan
rows.t: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whispers of Satan, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from their presence around me.

rows.title: Prayer After the Adhan
rows.t: O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the wasilah (a high status in Paradise) and the excellence (above all creation), and raise him to the praiseworthy station that You have promised him.

rows.title: Prayer for Forgiveness for Parents
rows.t: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and all the believers on the Day the account is established.

rows.title: Dua Seeking Good In This World And In The Hereafter
rows.t: Our Lord! Give us good in this world and give us good in the Hereafter, and save us from the torment of the hell fire.

rows.title: Dua To Make Heart Firm Upon Deen #1
rows.t: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.

rows.title: Dua To Make Heart Firm Upon Deen #2
rows.t: O Allah! Controller of the hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience.

rows.title: Dua To Make Heart Firm Upon Deen #3
rows.t: O our Lord, do not make our hearts incline to error after You have guided us.

rows.title: Dua To Seek Refuge Against The Loss Of Pleasure
rows.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the loss of the pleasures that You have bestowed, from changes in the health that You have bestowed, from Your sudden torment, and from all Your wrath.

rows.title: Dua To Resist Affliction
rows.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from severe calamity, being overtaken by misery, evil destiny, and the triumphant mockery of enemies.

rows.title: Dua To Be Released From Debt, Anxiety, Weakness, Laziness, Fear, And Pressure from Others
rows.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from care and grief, I seek refuge in You from incapacity and slackness, I seek refuge in You from cowardice and niggardliness, and I seek refuge in You from being overcome by debt and being put in subjection by men.

rows.title: Dua When Getting Good News
rows.t: Praise be to Allah, by whose grace goodness is perfected.

rows.title: Salat al-Ibrahimiyyah
rows.t: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. The salawat the Companions were taught when they asked how to send blessings upon him ﷺ. Recited in the final sitting of every prayer.

rows.title: The blessing joined to it
rows.t: O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

rows.title: Salawat on his household
rows.t: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his wives and his offspring, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim; and bless Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

rows.title: After the adhan
rows.t: O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the prayer about to be established, grant Muhammad the means and the excellence, and raise him to the praised station You have promised him. Said on hearing the adhan. The narration attaches intercession on the Day of Rising to whoever says it.

rows.title: Ten in return for one
rows.t: Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends blessings upon him ten times over.

rows.title: Tasbih after every prayer
rows.t: Glory be to Allah. All praise is for Allah. Allah is the greatest.

rows.title: Completing the hundred
rows.t: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is capable of all things.

rows.title: Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih
rows.t: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him. Said a hundred times in a day, the narration states his sins are removed though they be like the foam of the sea.

rows.title: The two light words
rows.t: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; glory be to Allah the Magnificent. Light on the tongue, heavy on the scales, beloved to the Most Merciful.

rows.title: Sayyid al-Istighfar
rows.t: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant. I keep Your covenant and Your promise as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me — for none forgives sins but You. Called the most excellent manner of seeking forgiveness. Said morning and evening.

rows.title: Seeking forgiveness
rows.t: I seek Allah’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.

rows.title: The treasure of Paradise
rows.t: There is no might nor power except with Allah. Described in the narration as a treasure from the treasures of Paradise.

rows.title: The comprehensive dua
rows.t: But among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire

rows.title: Ayat of steadfastness
rows.t: And when they went forth to [face] Goliath and his soldiers, they said, "Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people

rows.title: What we can bear
rows.t: Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people

rows.title: That hearts not swerve
rows.t: [Who say], "Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower

rows.title: Zakariyya: for offspring
rows.t: At that, Zechariah called upon his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication

rows.title: Sufficient is Allah
rows.t: Those to whom hypocrites said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it [merely] increased them in faith, and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs

rows.title: Adam: we have wronged ourselves
rows.t: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers

rows.title: Musa: expand my breast
rows.t: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance] And ease for me my task And untie the knot from my tongue That they may understand my speech

rows.title: Increase me in knowledge
rows.t: So high [above all] is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muhammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge

rows.title: Ayyub: adversity has touched me
rows.t: And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and you are the Most Merciful of the merciful

rows.title: Yunus: in the darknesses
rows.t: And [mention] the man of the fish, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers

rows.title: Zakariyya: leave me not alone
rows.t: And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while you are the best of inheritors

rows.title: Coolness of the eyes
rows.t: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous

rows.title: Musa: in need of good
rows.t: So he watered [their flocks] for them; then he went back to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need

rows.title: Ibrahim: keeper of prayer
rows.t: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established

rows.title: Ayat al-Kursi
rows.t: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great Recited after every obligatory prayer, and on lying down.

rows.title: The closing of al-Baqarah
rows.t: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people The narration states that whoever recites these two at night, they suffice him.

rows.title: Surah al-Ikhlas
rows.t: Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One Allah, the Eternal Refuge He neither begets nor is born Nor is there to Him any equivalent

rows.title: Surah al-Falaq
rows.t: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak From the evil of that which He created And from the evil of darkness when it settles And from the evil of the blowers in knots And from the evil of an envier when he envies

rows.title: Surah an-Nas
rows.t: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind The Sovereign of mankind The God of mankind From the evil of the retreating whisperer Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind From among the jinn and mankind

rows.title: The perfect words
rows.t: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.

rows.title: Nothing harms with His name
rows.t: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

rows.title: Upon Him I rely
rows.t: Allah is sufficient for me. There is no god but Him. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.

rows.title: The Talbiyah
rows.t: Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Truly all praise, favour and dominion are Yours. You have no partner. Said from entering ihram until the stoning of Jamrat al-ʿAqabah.

rows.title: During tawaf, between the two corners
rows.t: But among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire

rows.title: On climbing as-Safa
rows.t: Indeed as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. Recited on approaching as-Safa to begin the saʿy.

rows.title: Standing at as-Safa and al-Marwah
rows.t: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is capable of all things. There is no god but Allah alone: He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone.

rows.title: The day of ʿArafah
rows.t: The best supplication is the supplication of the Day of ʿArafah.

rows.title: In distress
rows.t: There is no god but Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the Noble Throne.

rows.title: Setting out on a journey
rows.t: Glory to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have accomplished it. And indeed to our Lord we will return.

rows.title: Leaving the house
rows.t: In the name of Allah, I rely upon Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah.

rows.title: Entering the masjid
rows.t: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

rows.title: Leaving the masjid
rows.t: O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.

rows.title: When rain falls
rows.t: A beneficial downpour.

rows.title: Visiting the sick
rows.t: No harm, it is a purification, if Allah wills.

rows.title: Asking for a cure
rows.t: Remove the harm, Lord of mankind. Heal — You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves behind no illness.

rows.title: Under the weight of debt
rows.t: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and enrich me by Your bounty so I need none besides You.

rows.title: Anxiety and grief
rows.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from miserliness and cowardice, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by men.

rows.title: Seeking guidance — Istikharah
rows.t: O Allah, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge, and Your power by Your might, and I ask You of Your immense bounty. For You are able and I am not, You know and I do not, and You are the Knower of all that is hidden. Prayed as two rakʿahs outside the obligatory prayers, then this said.

rows.title: When angry
rows.t: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan.

rows.title: Lying down to sleep
rows.t: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

rows.title: On waking
rows.t: All praise is for Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.

rows.title: For someone who marries
rows.t: May Allah bless you, and send blessings upon you, and join you both in goodness.

rows.title: In hardship and toil
rows.t: O Allah, there is no life but the life of the Hereafter.
